exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Talking about Coming of Age
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: Tom, when do you think a person really becomes an adult?
Tom: In my country, eighteen is the age when you get adult rights.
Mia: That's interesting. Here in Korea, we celebrate it at nineteen.
Tom: Do you have a special ceremony for it?
Mia: Yes. On Coming-of-Age Day, we bow to our parents to thank them.
Tom: That sounds lovely. We don't have one single ceremony.
Mia: So how do young people in your country mark it?
Tom: Many just have a big birthday party with family and friends.
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 问 Tom 何时算真正成年;Tom 说他的国家十八岁拥有成年权利;Mia 说韩国在十九岁庆祝、有成人日,要向父母鞠躬致谢;Tom 说他的国家没有单一的仪式,年轻人多是和家人朋友办大型生日派对。

questions.stem: At what age does Tom's country give adult rights?
At what age does Korea celebrate coming of age?
What do young Koreans do on Coming-of-Age Day?
Does Tom's country have one single ceremony?
How do many young people in Tom's country mark the day?

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 Coming-of-Age Day in Korea
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In South Korea, the third Monday of May is Coming-of-Age Day.
It celebrates the young people who turn nineteen that year.
Reaching this age means they can enjoy the rights of an adult.
At the ceremony, the young adults bow to their parents.
The bow is a way of saying thank you for their care.
exercises.translation_cn: 在韩国,五月的第三个星期一是成人日;它庆祝当年满十九岁的年轻人;到这个年龄意味着他们能享有成年人的权利;在仪式上,年轻人向父母鞠躬;这一鞠躬是为了感谢父母的关爱。

questions.stem: When is Coming-of-Age Day in Korea?
Who does the day celebrate?
What does reaching this age mean?
What do the young adults do at the ceremony?
What does the bow show?

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Planning a Homecoming
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Ben: Lily, our school's homecoming week is coming. Are you joining in?
Lily: Of course! I love the parade through the town the most.
Ben: Me too. The school band and the classic cars are great.
Lily: Have you heard who will be the Homecoming King and Queen?
Ben: Not yet. The election is being held this Friday.
Lily: Right. And the younger students form the Court, don't they?
Ben: Yes. There's also a dance at the end of the week.
Lily: I can't wait. It brings the whole school together.
exercises.translation_cn: Ben 问 Lily 是否参加学校的返校周;Lily 最爱穿过城镇的游行;Ben 也喜欢乐队和老爷车;Lily 问谁会当返校节国王和王后;Ben 说选举周五举行,低年级学生组成随从队伍;周末还有舞会;两人都期待它让全校齐聚一堂。

questions.stem: What does Lily like most about homecoming?
What does Ben like in the parade?
options: The school band and classic cars.

questions.stem: When is the election held?
Who forms the Court?
What happens at the end of the week?

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 Birthday Customs Around the World
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Different cultures have their own birthday customs.
In Finland, every new mother is given a baby box by the government.
In some Chinese families, a one-year-old baby chooses an object.
The item the baby reaches for is said to show its future.
These customs vary, but they all welcome a child with love.
exercises.translation_cn: 不同文化有各自的生日习俗;在芬兰,政府给每位新妈妈一个婴儿盒;在一些中国家庭,周岁婴儿要抓一件物品;婴儿抓到的东西据说预示其未来;这些习俗各不相同,但都满怀爱意地迎接孩子。

questions.stem: What does the passage talk about?
What does the government in Finland give new mothers?
What does a one-year-old Chinese baby do?
What is the item said to show?
What do all these customs do?

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Writing an Introduction
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Zhou: Miss Lee, I have to write an introduction to a Chinese ceremony. Any advice?
Miss Lee: Good. First choose one custom you really know well.
Zhou: I'd like to write about the old hair-pinning ceremony for girls.
Miss Lee: Nice choice. Start with a clear topic sentence.
Zhou: And then add some details about the time and the meaning?
Miss Lee: Exactly. Every sentence should support that one main idea.
Zhou: Should I finish with a concluding sentence?
Miss Lee: Yes. It should echo the topic and tie everything together.
exercises.translation_cn: 周同学请 Lee 老师指点如何写中国仪式的介绍;老师建议先选一个最熟悉的习俗;周想写古代女孩的笄礼;老师说先写明确的主题句;再补充时间和意义等细节;每句都要支持中心;最后用一个回扣主题、收束全文的结尾句。

questions.stem: What does Zhou have to write?
options: An introduction to a Chinese ceremony.

questions.stem: What should Zhou choose first?
Which custom does Zhou want to write about?
What should every sentence do?
What should the concluding sentence do?
options: Echo the topic and tie things together.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 A Tip for a Good Presentation
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple tip for giving a good presentation about customs.
A strong opening should catch your audience's attention at once.
You can begin by asking the audience a clever question.
Then tell them clearly what your main topic will be.
A good start makes your listeners want to hear more.
exercises.translation_cn: 这里有个做好习俗主题演讲的小贴士:好的开场要立刻抓住听众的注意力;你可以先向听众抛出一个巧妙的问题;接着清楚地告诉他们你的主题;一个好的开头会让听众想听下去。

questions.stem: What is this tip about?
What should a strong opening do?
How can you begin the presentation?
What should you do after the opening?
What does a good start do?
options: Makes listeners want to hear more.
